name: Cool-running chip wiring
subtitle: chip wires that carry current without heating up

effects.effect: some crystals conduct only along their surface, where nothing scatters the current

effect: some crystals conduct only along their surface, where nothing scatters the current
how: Data centres use a growing share of the world's electricity, and much of a chip's heat comes from forcing current through tiny copper wires where electrons keep bouncing off flaws. Wires made of a crystal that conducts only along its surface send electrons down lanes where they cannot bounce backwards, so the wiring runs cool even as it shrinks.
obstacle: Truly loss-free surface currents have only been seen near absolute zero; at room temperature the gain over copper is still unproven.
why: Topological wires are studied for chips; none replaces copper anywhere.
real: Simulations (Philip et al. 2016) and patents claim topological-insulator interconnects beat copper below ~6 nm; no demonstrated chip wiring.
